subject: Urgent: Mercury Retail — p99 regression & retry storm investigation
participants_external: alice@merchretail.com (Alice Grant, Head of Platform, Mercury Retail)
summary: Customer reported p99 latency spikes that materially impacted order throughput. Initial investigation shows client SDK timeouts and aggressive retry behavior produced request storms which amplified queueing on the Hosted API and caused p95/p99 regressions. Immediate mitigations applied (soft rate limit + temporary routing policy); follow-ups include SDK backoff defaults and a permanent server-side circuit breaker and improved observability on per-client retry bursts.
messages:
From: Alice Grant <alice@merchretail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes affecting checkout (~08:00-09:30 PST)

Rishi —

We started seeing sustained p99 spikes on Redwood hosted API starting ~08:05 PST this morning. Checkout calls are timing out for a subset of customers (500s + long tail p99 > 8s). We rolled back a change on our side and didn't see an immediate improvement. Attached is the p99 dashboard screenshot and a few sample request ids. Impact: several orders failed/retried, site checkout throughput down ~12%. This is high priority for us — please advise next steps and whether this looks like a Redwood-side regression.

Attachment: p99_dashboard.png

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Platform — Mercury Retail

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Grant <alice@merchretail.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes affecting checkout (~08:00-09:30 PST)

Alice —

Thank you for the quick flag and the screenshots. We're opening an urgent investigation and I’ve looped in SRE (Sergio) and the infra lead (Neha). Marissa from CS is on standby for customer comms.

Immediate plan:
- Stand up a short bridge for triage (we'll DM a link).
- Pull service-side latency + queueing + per-client connection counts.
- Check our routing/failover and any in-flight deploys.

Can you share any SDK versions you saw in the sample request IDs? If you can’t, ops@merchretail, please drop a line with the top IP ranges hitting us.

I'll push an interim status within 30m. Sorry for the disruption — we treat Mercury as high priority.

—Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes affecting checkout (~08:00-09:30 PST) — initial telemetry

Team —

I pulled the traces and inbound request histograms for the timeframe Alice provided. Quick findings:
- We see a sharp spike in total inbound QPS from 08:06–08:48 PST with a skewed tail: 95% of extra traffic originates from ~18 client certificates / IP ranges associated with Mercury.
- Many of the requests showing high CPU/latency have the same user-agent: "merch-sdk/1.3.2 (+https://merch.example)".
- Sampled logs show repeated timeouts on short-lived upstream connections followed by immediate retries (no exponential backoff). The retry arrival pattern looks like a classic retry storm — bursts every 2–3s.

Attached: sdk-log-samples.txt (sanitized request ids + timestamps)

Immediate mitigation I recommend:
1) Apply a soft, per-customer concurrency limit (throttle) for Mercury for 30m to prevent queue depth explosion.
2) Enable quick 429-based circuit break to encourage client backoff.
3) Pull SDK logs from Mercury to confirm retry/backoff config.

I can roll the throttle in staging now and promote to prod if we see positive effects.

—Sergio
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes — root-cause summary and recommended fixes

Folks —

I completed a deeper analysis of traces + KV cache stats + runtime queues. TL;DR: the service itself did not have a code regression, but observed p95/p99 regressed because client-side short timeouts and aggressive retry semantics created concentrated bursts that overloaded request processing lanes and caused increased tail latency. Key evidence:
- Latency heatmap correlates strongly with windows where retry bursts arrive (see attached investigation_notes.md).
- Kernel / process queues grew by ~3x during bursts; CPU saturation occurred on a subset of GPUs serving Mercury, increasing serialization delays on IO.
- The SDK version in sampled requests (merch-sdk/1.3.2) defaults to a 3s client timeout and linear retry every 2s — no jitter and no exponential backoff.

Recommended action plan (short & medium term):
Short (minutes-hours)
- Apply per-customer soft concurrency caps and 429 backoff for offending certs/IPs (I can patch rate_limit_patch.diff and push).
- Roll a temporary routing policy to shift a slice of Mercury traffic to a slightly overprovisioned pool (to prevent collateral impact).
- Offer immediate credits for failed orders (coordinate with Marissa).

Medium (days)
- Publish an SDK advisory and release patch to default to exponential backoff + jitter and increase client-side timeout to 15–20s. Jordan, can you own the SDK advisory?
- Implement a server-side circuit breaker and per-client retry detection metric so we can throttle at the edge before it hits internal queues.
- Improve per-customer telemetry in Console (retry burst alerts).

I will attach the investigation notes and a short checklist for the ops runbook.

Attachments: investigation_notes.md, rate_limit_patch.diff

—Neha
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Grant <alice@merchretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Update: Immediate mitigations applied and next steps

Alice —

Thank you for your patience. Quick update and what we did in the last 6 hours: 
- We applied a temporary soft concurrency cap on Mercury traffic and enabled 429 backoff. Early telemetry shows tail latency improved and queue depth flattened within ~12 minutes of the change.
- We shifted a small % of traffic to an overprovisioned pool to reduce noisy-neighbor effects.
- Our infra team will publish a formal SDK advisory recommending upgrading to merch-sdk/1.3.3 (backoff + jitter) and increasing default client timeout to 15–20s. Jordan will coordinate this with your platform team.

Immediate asks for Mercury:
1) Please validate your SDK version and, if possible, schedule an upgrade to 1.3.3 today.
2) Share any internal routing or proxy configs that could be applying short timeouts on your side.

We’ll follow up with a post-incident report and a proposed credit for impacted orders. Marissa will coordinate the customer-facing credit.

—Rishi

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Exec brief: Mercury Retail p99 incident — summary & ask

Laura / Leadership —

Brief summary of the Mercury incident (12/15):
- Impact: p99 latency spikes and increased error rate for Mercury between 08:05–09:00 PST; checkout throughput dropped ~12% during the window. Customer reported timeouts and retries.
- Root cause: No server-side code regression. Client SDK defaults (short timeouts + linear immediate retries) led to a retry storm that amplified queueing pressures and caused tail latency regressions on a subset of serving nodes.
- Actions taken: soft per-customer concurrency cap + 429 backoff applied (rolled back after stabilization window), traffic slice moved to overprovisioned pool, SDK advisory drafted.

Requests / asks:
1) Approve up to $15k in one-time credits for impacted orders (Marissa to finalize).
2) Approve prioritization of server-side circuit breaker work to detect and preempt retry storms (estimated 3 sprints; Neha to provide scoping).
3) Greenlight a public SDK advisory and a point release that enforces better backoff behavior by default (Jordan to run).

I recommend we treat this as a process & product gap: SDK defaults should be safer for production and Console should surface retry-burst alerts per-customer.

Happy to walk through telemetry — attaching the condensed incident link and notes.

—Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts
